cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The Task 1 classification contract test was collected before the new classification_contracts module existed.
impact: RED was observed at test collection with ModuleNotFoundError; no production implementation existed yet.
lesson: Write strict classification contract tests before implementing the public API and preserve the fail-closed information-set boundary.

cause: Task 2 through Task 9 RED tests were collected before their new package-local modules and split/preprocessing seams existed.
impact: The expected missing-module/import failures proved the new tests were not passing accidentally; no unrelated files were changed.
lesson: Keep split, preprocessing, adapter, metric, protocol, explanation and projection tests ahead of their implementations.

cause: The first frontend test command was run from the repository root rather than the frontend package directory.
impact: npm reported package.json missing at the root; no product failure was established and the command will be rerun from frontend.
lesson: Run frontend gates from the frontend package directory exactly as declared in the Work Order.

cause: The focused classification consumer test imports classification_graph_nodes before the required owned-path graph projection helper exists.
impact: The classification consumer suite stops at collection; no consumer assertion runs until the graph projection seam is implemented.
lesson: Keep the Graph projection typed and package-local before running the consumer evidence suite.

cause: The first full focused run exposed three implementation mismatches: sklearn 1.9 Brier uses y_proba, panel_new_entity validates period support before the required entity-overlap invariant, and classification artifact persistence writes the payload under a fixed key instead of preserving artifact names.
impact: Five assertions failed across metrics, protocol, leakage ordering, and persistence; 20 classification assertions passed and no protected path was touched.
lesson: Run the complete focused suite after each TDD slice and preserve environment-specific numerical API contracts, invariant ordering, and artifact identity.

cause: After the Brier API compatibility fix, ROC AUC on a single-class sample returned a non-finite value and the generic metric wrapper emitted only 'non-finite metric' instead of a class-support reason.
impact: One protocol metric assertion failed; the remaining eight protocol assertions passed.
lesson: Undefined metrics need precondition-specific reasons and must not be normalized into a generic numeric failure.

cause: The new renderer exposed serialized metric keys verbatim, so 'accuracy' was rendered instead of the contract-facing label 'Accuracy'.
impact: One of two focused renderer assertions failed; the source existed and the blocked-reason test passed.
lesson: Typed consumer renderers should preserve values while applying stable human-readable labels at the presentation boundary.

cause: The renderer used String.replaceAll and an unannotated replacement callback while the frontend TypeScript lib is ES2020 with strict checking.
impact: Focused renderer tests passed, but frontend typecheck failed on the new owned source.
lesson: Keep package-local renderer code within the repository's declared ES2020 and strict TypeScript surface.

cause: The frontend classification contract test was created before its same-line ClassificationEvidence renderer source.

evidence.ref: frontend ClassificationEvidence focused test and typecheck before source completion

impact: Consumer Projection frontend typecheck could not resolve the owned renderer module until this line supplied it.
lesson: Keep package-local renderer source and contract tests in the same implementation slice before handing the path to another line.

cause: The new typed consumer, clarification and additive-entrypoint tests were collected before the corresponding owned entrypoint and contract helper existed.
impact: The consumer suite stopped at collection on the missing additive classification entrypoint; this is the intended RED state for the next implementation slice.
lesson: Add Task 8-9 contract tests before implementing package-local registry, clarification and additive prediction seams.

cause: The provider catalog smoke command was launched from backend with .venv/bin/python instead of the repository interpreter path ../.venv/bin/python.

evidence.ref: provider catalog smoke command from backend

impact: The smoke command did not execute; no provider catalog conclusion was drawn from it.
lesson: Use the declared repository interpreter and PYTHONPATH from the active package directory for every backend gate.

cause: The classification split kernel recorded cross-partition label-window overlaps and embargo declarations but did not mutate affected development assignments to a non-training purged partition.
impact: Two adversarial leakage assertions failed; the current implementation could otherwise retain rows that must be excluded from development evidence.
lesson: Purge and embargo contracts must change executable partition membership, not only describe a receipt after the split is built.

cause: Adversarial protocol tests exposed that HoldoutSealGuard accepted an unknown metric release request and the protocol did not yet emit development OOF calibration or negative-control receipts.
impact: Two protocol assertions failed; holdout access semantics and evidence completeness were not yet sufficient for closeout.
lesson: Seal release plans must be closed over known metrics, and model outputs need explicit OOF calibration/control evidence before they are projected.

cause: The first negative-control implementation globally permuted development labels, which could remove a class from a CV training complement even though the original split manifest was stratified.
impact: The protocol could not compute a declared permuted-target control under strict fold class-support checks.
lesson: Negative controls must preserve the declared exchangeability unit and executable fold support; never weaken adapter training invariants to force a control through.

cause: The focused test command used a stale ../.venv/bin/python path from the worktree and the fallback python alias is unavailable; the test process did not start.

evidence.ref: PYTHONPATH=$PWD ../.venv/bin/python -m pytest ...; PYTHONPATH=backend python scripts/devline_control.py append --help

impact: Focused verification was delayed until the worktree-local .venv interpreter was located.
lesson: Run repository verification with the resolved worktree-local interpreter and record path failures before retrying.

cause: The focused test command used ../tests from the worktree root, but this linked worktree is nested two levels below the repository root and the test suite is at ../../tests.
impact: The test process did not start; no code result was produced.
lesson: Resolve test paths relative to the active worktree layout before running verification.

cause: The next retry assumed the tests were two levels above the active worktree, but this worktree contains its own tests directory and the requested file is at ./tests.
impact: The test process again did not start; verification remained pending.
lesson: Use the active worktree's own owned tests path when it exists; do not infer a shared-root test location from another execution context.

cause: When a deterministic within-fold label derangement was impossible, the protocol appended the typed BLOCKED control receipt but skipped the base model evidence record; later holdout selection indexed a missing model entry and raised KeyError.
impact: The required blocked-control path did not return a valid protocol result and could not produce a legal control receipt.
lesson: Record validated model OOF/selection evidence independently of optional negative-control computation; a blocked control must not erase the primary model record.

cause: The new blocked-control test assumed ClassificationSplitManifestV1.to_dict exposed content_hash, but the hash is a computed property and is intentionally only placed in the protocol/control receipt.
impact: The negative-control test failed at its receipt assertion after the implementation path returned; no production failure remained at that point.
lesson: Assert computed manifest identity through the public receipt contract rather than an absent serialized field.

cause: Adding the package-local classification provider changed built-in catalog provider_ids order so it no longer satisfied the existing sorted deterministic catalog contract.
impact: The old regression/contract-lock suite reported one failure even though 178 tests passed; catalog determinism evidence was not acceptable for closeout.
lesson: Package-local provider declarations must preserve the loader's deterministic provider ordering contract without changing central routing.

cause: The repository builtin catalog currently contains pre-existing consumer_projection and data_consumer manifests whose filename-derived provider order is already inconsistent with the contract-lock assertion; the classification manifest cannot repair that relative ordering without changing another line or central loader.

evidence.ref: full old suite: 178 passed, 1 failed at test_catalog_load_order_and_digest_are_deterministic; excluding known case: 178 passed, 1 deselected

impact: The full old contract-lock command is 178 passed, 1 failed at catalog order; the failure is retained as a cross-line gate gap and the test passes when that known case is excluded.
lesson: Keep cross-line provider catalog ordering gaps explicit and out of the classification owned path; do not modify parallel provider manifests or central routing to hide the mismatch.

cause: The classification lane focused contract, protocol, leakage, consumer, purge/embargo, and strict negative-control tests completed successfully.
impact: Lane-local backend correctness evidence is available for handoff.
lesson: Keep focused numerical, leakage, and consumer evidence separate from deferred integration gates.

cause: The classification mutation/negative subset passed, including actual purge/embargo partition removal, holdout sealing, unknown adapter/metric rejection, and strict fold-support derangement blocking.

evidence.ref: classification focused suite -k 'rejects or invalid or blocked or incomplete or missing or violation or requires or purges or embargo or single or unsupported or unknown or sealed or repeated or derangement'

impact: Adversarial evidence supports fail-closed behavior and does not relax adapter or fold-support constraints.
lesson: A legal negative-control receipt or typed BLOCKED/insufficient reason is the accepted terminal evidence when exchangeability support is insufficient.

cause: The unmounted ClassificationEvidence renderer tests and frontend TypeScript typecheck completed successfully.

evidence.ref: cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/report/ClassificationEvidence.test.tsx && npm run typecheck

impact: Owned renderer source is complete and is not left for another line; actual mount/browser acceptance remains outside this lane.
lesson: Treat package-local renderer correctness separately from production mount and browser evidence.

cause: Owned classification Python modules compiled successfully and git diff --check reported no whitespace errors.

evidence.ref: PYTHONPATH=backend .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q <owned classification modules>; git diff --check

impact: Source-level syntax and diff hygiene evidence is available; full release compilation/gate remains deferred.
lesson: Keep compile/diff checks distinct from browser, cutover, and full release acceptance.

cause: Final scope review compared classification-owned paths with the protected Agent/Notebook/evidence/routing/UI mount paths and the parallel Data Consumer files.

evidence.ref: git diff --name-only; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; protected-path review

impact: No classification change was made to central Agent/Notebook routing, Context Compiler, ReportView, sectionRegistry, protected data-consumer paths, or the central provider loader.
lesson: Close the line with explicit disjoint-path evidence and retain unrelated cross-line gates as open rather than masking them.

cause: The classification owned implementation, focused and negative-control tests, renderer/typecheck, compile/diff checks, handoff, formal verification, and retrospective are complete; the cross-line catalog order gate is explicitly retained as an open GAP.
impact: The formal classification development line can be indexed as completed without claiming deferred cutover, browser, full-gate, or release evidence.
lesson: Complete a formal line only after lane-local evidence and explicit deferred boundaries are recorded in the handoff and verified event stream.
